clinical_knowledge.topic: Hemorrhagic ovarian cyst or ruptured ovarian cyst (r/o ectopic pregnancy) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Hemorrhagic ovarian cyst or ruptured ovarian cyst (r/o ectopic pregnancy) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Hemorrhagic Ovarian Cyst or Ovarian Cyst Rupture, differential includes ectopic pregnancy, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: sudden left-sided pelvic pain, mild nausea, and history of ovarian cyst

Key HPI features: 24F reports sudden, sharp pain in her left lower abdomen that started 4 hours ago. Pain is constant, accompanied by mild nausea. Denies vaginal bleeding. Missed her period 2 weeks ago.

Objective/Exam findings: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Hemorrhagic Ovarian Cyst or Ovarian Cyst Rupture, differential includes ectopic pregnancy.
Relevant background/PMH: Left ovarian cyst diagnosed on ultrasound 1 year ago
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Hemorrhagic ovarian cyst or ruptured ovarian cyst (r/o ectopic pregnancy).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Ectopic pregnancy without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Missed period (rule out pregnancy).
management_principles: Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Hemorrhagic Ovarian Cyst or Ovarian Cyst Rupture, differential includes ectopic pregnancy
Perform urine pregnancy test to evaluate for ectopic pregnancy, order pelvic ultrasound (evaluate for free pelvic fluid, adnexal mass)
Manage pain supportively if hemodynamically stable
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

must_ask.say: When was your last period, and could you be pregnant?

must_ask.objective: Characterize the pain onset and quality
must_ask.say: Did the pain start suddenly, and how would you describe it?
You mentioned a cyst before — do you know which side and how large it was?
Have you felt dizzy or faint since the pain started?
Have you had any vaginal bleeding or spotting?

history.answer: I came to the clinic because of sudden, sharp pain in my lower left belly that started four hours ago, and I feel nauseous.
It hit me completely out of the blue about four hours ago while I was studying at my desk, and it has been constant ever since.
The pain started in my lower left abdomen and has stayed right there. It has not spread anywhere else.
No, it doesn't shoot to my back, shoulder, or down to my groin. It stays right in my lower left side.
It is a sharp, constant ache. It does not squeeze or come and go in waves.
It is quite severe, about a seven out of ten, and it hasn't eased up since it began.
Walking or moving around definitely makes it hurt worse, so I prefer to lie completely still. Resting doesn't make it go away, though.
I've had mild cramping on that side occasionally during my periods, but never anything sudden or intense like this.
I have felt nauseous ever since the pain came on, but I haven't actually thrown up.
My bowel movements are normal. I went to the bathroom normally this morning, I can pass gas, and there is no diarrhea or blood.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or cold sweats.
No, my eyes and skin are not yellow, and my urine has not been dark or tea-colored.
No, I have no pain or burning when I urinate, no blood in my urine, and I'm not going more frequently than usual.
No, I haven't felt dizzy, lightheaded, or like I was going to pass out, even when I stood up.
No, I don't have any vaginal bleeding, spotting, or unusual discharge.
No, I don't have any chest pain, tightness, or shortness of breath.
I only ate a regular sandwich for lunch today. I didn't eat anything greasy or heavy, and I haven't had any alcohol.
I took one acetaminophen tablet about two hours ago, but it didn't really help. I haven't taken aspirin or ibuprofen.
No, I've never had heart rhythm problems, palpitations, blood clots, or vascular disease.
Yes, about a year ago, an ultrasound showed a cyst on my left ovary. The doctor told me it was small and just needed monitoring.
I'm wondering if that ovarian cyst ruptured, or if maybe this could be appendicitis even though it's on my left side.
I'm really worried that there might be bleeding inside my abdomen.
I would like to get a pelvic ultrasound or scan today so we can find out what happened.
Aside from the ovarian cyst found last year, I don't have any chronic illnesses or conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and I've never been admitted to a hospital.
I don't take any regular prescription medications, birth control pills, or herbal supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or anything else.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used electronic cigarettes.
I only drink socially, maybe one glass of wine or beer once or twice a month, but none recently.
I'm a graduate student, and I live in an apartment near the university with a roommate.
Both of my parents are healthy, and there is no family history of ovarian or gynecological diseases.
I am sexually active with my boyfriend.
My periods are usually regular every 28 days, but my last period was six weeks ago, so I am about two weeks late.
We usually use condoms, but we haven't used them every single time.
Because my period is two weeks late, I realize I could be pregnant, though I haven't taken a home pregnancy test yet.

exam.finding: Alert young female lying still on the examination table in moderate discomfort from lower abdominal pain.
Blood pressure 115/75 mmHg, heart rate 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor; sclerae are clear and non-icteric.
Abdomen is flat and symmetric without surgical scars, distension, or visible peristalsis.
Normal active bowel sounds heard throughout all four quadrants; no bruits.
Soft abdomen with localized moderate tenderness in the left lower quadrant without rigidity; no tenderness in the right lower quadrant or upper abdomen.
Mild localized rebound tenderness in the left lower quadrant; negative in all other quadrants.
Negative McBurney point tenderness, negative Rovsing sign, and negative psoas and obturator signs.
Negative Murphy sign with no tenderness elicited in the right upper quadrant during deep inspiration.
Moderate tenderness elicited in the left adnexal region without cervical motion tenderness; no vaginal blood or abnormal discharge seen.
